entities.summary:
Lie Yukou was a Chinese philosopher who is considered the author of the Daoist book Liezi, which uses his honorific name Liezi.

Born in unknown and dying at 374 BCE, Lie Yukou was a prominent figure in the development of Daoist thought. His philosophical ideas had a significant impact on the Chinese intellectual scene of the time, particularly in the areas of ethics and governance.

Lie Yukou's most famous work, Liezi, was a collection of anecdotes and philosophical musings that explored the nature of reality, morality, and the human condition. The book's emphasis on individualism, spontaneity, and the pursuit of wisdom resonated with many Chinese thinkers of the Classical period.

Despite his significant contributions to Chinese philosophy, Lie Yukou's life and work are not as well-documented as those of other prominent figures of the time. However, his influence on Daoist thought and his legacy as a key figure in the development of Chinese philosophy cannot be overstated.
